hosts.name: Linda Carducci
hosts.bio: Linda Carducci is the weekday morning host on WETA Classical. She received classical training on piano and hosted a daily classical music program in Pittsburgh prior to coming to WETA.

hosts.name: Bill Bukowski
hosts.bio: Bill Bukowski is the weekday midday host on WETA Classical. He came to WETA in 2013 from WSCL on the Delmarva pennisula. In his spare time he enjoys playing guitar, mountain dulcimer and ukulele.

hosts.name: Nicole Lacroix
hosts.bio: Nicole Lacroix is the weekday afternoon host on WETA Classical. Lacroix spent fifteen years at the former WGMS in Washington, with stints at VOA, KDFC San Francisco and at Baltimore's WJHU and WBJC.

hosts.name: James Jacobs
hosts.bio: James Jacobs can be heard evenings on WETA Classical. His varied career has included performing on programs like A Prairie Home Companion and working as a producer for both recorded programs and concert broadcasts.

hosts.name: John Banther
hosts.bio: John Banther is an on-air host and production manager at WETA Classical. He can be heard Monday evenings, when he hosts our weekly Front Row Washington broadcast.

hosts.name: Rich Kleinfeldt
hosts.bio: Rich Kleinfeldt is the Sunday evening host on WETA Classical. A professional musician, teacher and lecturer, Rich also hosts Center Stage at Wolf Trap.

hosts.name: Evan Keely
hosts.bio: Evan Keely is a weekend host on WETA Classical. A composer, arranger and vocalist, he has a degree in Music History from the Boston University School of Music.

hosts.name: Austin Vitaliano
hosts.bio: Austin Vitaliano is a weekend host on WETA Classical. Austin is an active vocalist and performer based in the D.C. area.

hosts.name: Chip Brienza
hosts.bio: Chip Brienza is a fill-in host on WETA Classical. An actor as well as a broadcaster, Chip has many film and television credits on his resume.

hosts.name: Matthew Dayton
hosts.bio: Matthew Dayton is a weekend and fill-in host on WETA Classical. He is also a professional musician, composer, and teacher in Takoma Park, MD.

hosts.name: David Martosko
hosts.bio: David Martosko is a journalist and writer who was trained on the piano, cello, and tuba but sang his way through his teens and ultimately embraced opera — first on stage and then on the podium.

hosts.name: Marcus Pfeifer
hosts.bio: Marcus Pfeifer is a weekend host on WETA Classical. A native of Pittsburgh, PA, Marcus earned a degree in Music from the Indiana University of Pennsylvania.

hosts.name: Julie Huang Tucker
hosts.bio: Julie Huang Tucker is a fill-in host on WETA Classical. She is music director at First Presbyterian Church of Arlington and has performed as an organist at the Kennedy Center, Strathmore, and National Cathedral with such ensembles as the NSO and National Philharmonic.

hosts.name: Scott Tucker
hosts.bio: Scott Tucker is a weekend host at WETA. He is Professor Emeritus at Cornell University and Artistic Director Emeritus of the Choral Arts Society of Washington.

articles.title: Matthew White on WNO's Madama Butterfly
articles.dek: James Jacobs speaks with tenor Matthew White about the Washington National Opera's production of Puccini's Madama Butterfly.

articles.title: DC Composer James Lee III
articles.dek: Linda Carducci speaks with Maryland-based composer James Lee III about his visions and influences, his compositions, and his thoughts for the evolving nature of Classical music.

articles.title: Opera Lafayette Celebrates Rameau 350
articles.dek: James Jacobs speaks with Artistic Director of Opera Lafayette, Patrick Dupre Quigley, about their Rameau 350 project, starting with Les Surprises des l'Amour this month.

articles.title: Opera Lafayette Celebrates Rameau 350
articles.dek: James Jacobs speaks with Artistic Director of Opera Lafayette, Patrick Dupre Quigley, about their Rameau 350 project, starting with Les Surprises des l'Amour this month.

articles.title: DC Composer James Lee III
articles.dek: Linda Carducci speaks with Maryland-based composer James Lee III about his visions and influences, his compositions, and his thoughts for the evolving nature of Classical music.

articles.title: Matthew White on WNO's Madama Butterfly
articles.dek: James Jacobs speaks with tenor Matthew White about the Washington National Opera's production of Puccini's Madama Butterfly.

articles.title: Forward Thinking Opera Company IN Series' New Home in Southwest DC
articles.dek: Evan Keely speaks with IN Series Artistic Director Timothy Nelson about the exciting new chapter of a permanent home at Revada Performing Arts Center in SW DC.

articles.title: DC Composer Greg Sandow
articles.dek: James Jacobs speaks with DC-based composer Greg Sandow about his works and highlights his album "Three Quartets" recorded by Terra String Quartet.

articles.title: The Revada Arts Center: A brand-new home for the arts in Southwest DC
articles.dek: Nicole Lacroix speaks with Theater Alliance's executive artistic director Shanara Gabrielle about the opening of a new performing arts space in Southwest DC.

articles.title: Ariel Quartet Plays Late Beethoven
articles.dek: James Jacobs speaks with Ariel Quartet's violist Jan Grüning about completing their Beethoven cycle with their release of the third and final recording of Beethoven's string quartets.

articles.title: Actor Jamie Wilkes on Playing C.P.E. Bach on STC's The Score
articles.dek: James Jacobs speaks with actor Jamie Wilkes about playing C.P.E. Bach in STC's production of The Score, a play surrounding the musical challenge proposed to J.S. Bach resulting in the Musical Offering.

articles.title: Pulitzer Prize-Winning Ellen Taaffe Zwilich on Her Music
articles.dek: John Banther speaks with the first woman composer to win the Pulitzer Prize in Music, Ellen Taaffe Zwilich, about her music, including The Peanuts Gallery composed in honor of her feature on the comic strip.

articles.title: Damien Geter's Declaration with J'Nai Bridges and Sphinx Virtuosi at Anna H. Wang Concert Series
articles.dek: John Banther speaks with composer Damien Geter about his work Declarations, to be featured on an upcoming program with Anna H Wang Concert Series featuring Sphinx Virtuosi and J'Nai Bridges.

articles.title: Davóne Tines' Recital No. 1: Mass on Fortas Chamber Music Concerts
articles.dek: Bass-baritone Davóne Tines opens Fortas Chamber Music Concerts with Recital No. 1: MASS, both a recital and theatrical work exploring spirituality, history, identity and renewal.

articles.title: On Brahms and Bonds with The Thirteen's Matthew Robertson
articles.dek: Evan Keely and The Thirteen's Artistic Director Matthew Robertson share an insight into Brahms' German Requiem and Bond's Credo ahead of The Thirteen's first concert of the season, Brahms and Bonds.

programs.name: Choral Showcase
programs.desc: A wide variety of classical choral music from Washington and beyond — from perennial favorites to new discoveries, from Gregorian Chant to the present.

programs.name: Classical Breakdown
programs.desc: John Banther takes classical music fans behind the scenes with interviews, deep dives, and analysis. Episodes released bi-weekly on Tuesdays. Produced by WETA Classical in Washington, D.C.

programs.name: Classical Countdown
programs.desc: An annual WETA Classical tradition. Listeners vote for their favorite classical music pieces and we play back the top 100 pieces during Thanksgiving week.

programs.name: From The Top
programs.desc: Hear the next generation of classical champions as talented teens play the classics in concert.

programs.name: Front Row Washington
programs.desc: Classical performances by top local musicians and ensembles at venues throughout the Washington area.

programs.name: NSO Showcase
programs.desc: WETA Classical's ongoing series featuring performances from the National Symphony Orchestra, hosted by Nicole Lacroix. This special radio series is made possible by WETA's Friends of Classical Music, including Patricia Sagon. The National Symphony Orchestra’s radio programs are generously supported in part by The Morris and Gwendolyn Cafritz Foundation.

programs.name: Opera at Eight
programs.desc: In addition to the opera excerpts presented throughout the day, WETA VivaLaVoce features a complete opera at 8 pm each day: Opera at 8. These opera performances are taken from the extensive WETA Classical library, ranging from classic recordings to the most recent releases.

programs.name: Opera Encore
programs.desc: To accommodate our international listeners, WETA VivaLaVoce features a complete opera at 3 am ET each day. During this timeslot, we re-air the Opera at 8 broadcast from the previous month. So, operas featured one month at 8pm will be rebroadcast the following month at 3am.

programs.name: Opera Matinee
programs.desc: WETA Classical is Washington's home for opera year round. From December through early June, experience the power and passion of the Metropolitan Opera's Saturday Matinee Broadcasts. The rest of the year features performances from leading opera houses around the world.

programs.name: PBS News Hour
programs.desc: Millions of Americans turn to PBS for the solid, reliable reporting that has made PBS News Hour one of the most trusted news programs on television. WETA Classical is proud to simulcast our television broadcast at 7pm weekdays.

programs.name: Performance Today
programs.desc: Performance Today® features live concert recordings that can’t be heard anywhere else, highlights from new album releases, and in-studio performances and interviews. Performance Today® is based at the APM studios in St. Paul, Minnesota, but is frequently on the road, with special programs broadcast from festivals and public radio stations around the country.

programs.name: WETA Virtuoso Lunchtime Concert
programs.desc: Live recorded performances from the finest orchestras in the U.S. and around the world, Monday through Thursday from 12-2 PM. These Lunchtime Concerts showcase the artistry and energy of live performance and connect WETA Virtuoso listeners to concert halls across the globe. Fridays take a more intimate turn with chamber music followed by an exploration of early music, offering a perfect midday escape into classical music's diverse landscape.
